narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

This is Twist. 1950s–1960s.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in the late 1950s among teenagers in the United States, with roots in African American pelvic dance motions dating back to the 19th century.
Hank Ballard wrote the song 'The Twist' in 1959, but Chubby Checker’s 1960 performance on The Dick Clark Show is credited with launching the global craze.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a teenage fad, it became a social dance for all ages.
It is often viewed as a symbol of 1960s hedonism and the liberation of youth culture.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Kettlebell Lunge and Twist.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/21/Kettlebell_Lunge_and_Twist.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
The hips, torso, and legs rotate as a single unit while the feet grind back and forth on the floor.
Arms are held out from the body, bent at the elbows, and move independently of the lower body.
Watch for The Cigarette Grind.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (F9WxQDnFpWA)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Solo or crowd, requires minimal space.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is set to rock and roll music, typically in 4/4 time.
Key instruments include electric guitar, drums, bass, and saxophone.
Listen for the Electric guitar, Drums, Bass, Saxophone.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 120 beats a minute.
A high-energy, guitar-driven sound with a prominent, steady drum beat that encourages rhythmic hip movement.

narration: There is no specific costume, though it is associated with 1960s casual fashion.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Chubby Checker, Hank Ballard, Joey Dee and the Starliters, Bill Haley, and Dick Clark.
Variants include the 'Spanish Twist' and 'Florida Twist' in Latin America, and various localized adaptations in France and the Soviet Union.
Derived from rock and roll and earlier African American pelvic dances; influenced subsequent fad dances like the Monkey and the Watusi.

Twist is sibling of Watusi: Another fad dance inspired by the success of the Twist.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Bend knees slightly.
Footwork from the sources: Grinding the balls of the feet against the floor.
Drill: Practice hip swivels while standing still.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Rotate hips and torso as a single unit.
Step 4: Grind the balls of the feet against the floor as if putting out a cigarette.

on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Coordinate the feet with the hip rotation.
